summary:
What is it?
An interactive GIS platform that calculates the Planetary Similarity Index (PSI) to evaluate and compare any point on Earth with future base sites on the Moon or Mars.
How does it work?
It uses a weighted mathematical model based on five normalized geospatial variables (Terrain 30%, Geology 25%, Aridity 20%, Temperature 15%, and Subsoil 10%) connected with data from space agencies (NASA and ESA).
Why is it important?
It allows for objectively and scientifically identifying new test sites on Earth (like the El Pinacate Volcanic Field in Mexico), optimizing planning and training for future space exploration missions.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

It's an interactive GIS platform that calculates a Planetary Similarity Index (PSI) for any point on Earth. It uses a weighted mathematical model based on five normalized geospatial variables (Terrain 30%, Geology 25%, Aridity 20%, Temperature 15%, and Subsoil 10%) linked with orbital and global data from space agencies like NASA and ESA.

What are the benefits?

It allows you to objectively, scientifically, and reproducibly identify terrestrial analog sites (like the El Pinacate Volcanic Field in Mexico or the Atacama Desert in Chile) to conduct field tests, evaluate robotic mobility, and train space crews before real missions to the Moon or Mars.

What is the expected impact of the project?

Optimize planning and reduce the logistical costs of space missions by rigorously selecting the best testing environments on Earth, while also highlighting underrated analogous regions in Latin America and around the world.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

It was developed using interactive web maps with Leaflet, interface design with Tailwind CSS, multidimensional charts with Chart.js, spatial data processing and models in Python (Pandas, OpenPyXL), as well as geospatial databases from NASA and ESA (SRTM DEM, Landsat, Sentinel-2, LRO, MOLA).

How creative is your project?

It breaks from the traditional approach of relying solely on classic analogs (like Antarctica or Atacama) by proposing an automated, open GIS platform that evaluates any coordinate on the planet using a weighted mathematical formula and a side-by-side comparator with radar charts.

What factors did our team take into account?

We considered methodological accuracy (normalization of physical and climatic variables), operational feasibility and accessibility of terrestrial sites, integration of open and reliable data sources, and the strategic relevance of analytically highlighting regions rich in basalts and lava tubes, like Mexico.
